title: Mutable Quota Autoscaler and Fallback Playbook (PRD - draft)
summary: This PRD proposes a SLA-aware, mutable-quota autoscaler plus an operational fallback playbook for Dedicated capacity customers. The goal is to provide predictable tenant SLAs while allowing controlled, temporary burst behavior and graceful degradation under contention. Introduces a quota mutation model, demotion lanes, and an offline simulator for ops and SRE to validate policies before rollout.
problem_statement: Current Dedicated customers want predictable latency and throughput guarantees while also needing occasional bursts (traffic spikes, batch jobs, demos). Existing reserved capacity is rigid: either strictly enforced quotas (leading to failed requests during spikes) or permissive burst credits (which can cause noisy neighbors and SLA violations). We need a middle ground: SLO-driven autoscaling that adjusts tenants' effective quotas in real time, with deterministic fallback lanes and observable decisioning so customers and ops understand behavior.
goals: 1) Maintain tenant-level SLOs (p95 latency and error rate) for 'guaranteed' routes. 2) Allow short-lived bursts without manual ops intervention and without risking cross-tenant SLA violations. 3) Provide deterministic fallback paths that degrade predictably (e.g., reduced concurrency, queuing, lower-cost model variant). 4) Give ops a simulator and audit log to validate policies and for post-incident analysis.
non_goals: 1) This is not a multi-tenant security isolation project (no cryptographic separation changes). 2) Not addressing long-term capacity purchases or billing model changes here (billing implications documented but separate). 3) Not replacing Dedicated scheduler; the feature augments admissions and quota decisions at the request routing layer.
success_metrics:
- Percent of spikes absorbed without customer-visible errors (>90% target for spikes < 15 minutes).
- Reduction in cross-tenant SLA incidents by 60% within 3 months of rollout.
- Mean time to apply fallback lane after capacity breach <= 30s.
- Simulator match rate: >80% of production incidents simulated within +/- 20% of observed request rejections or latency increases.
requirements:
Functional:
- A runtime component (quota controller) that emits per-tenant mutable quotas in near real-time.
- Autoscaler that increases reserved capacity only when long-lived demand justifies it (avoid oscillation).
- Burst window policy language: duration, credit accrual, max burst multiplier.
- Fallback lanes: queuing, concurrency caps, model variant fallback, and admission tokens.
- Audit trail: reasons for quota mutations, timestamps, and impacted requests.
Non-functional:
- Decision latency under 200ms.
- Audit logs retained for at least 90 days in the control plane.
- SRE tooling to replay decisions in simulator with production traces.
Security/Compliance:
- Tenant quota metadata stored encrypted at rest.
- No cross-tenant data exposure in fallback behaviors.
Rolling constraints:
- Feature must be opt-in per customer for first release.
- Grace period controls available to customers via Console and API.
high_level_design: The system has three coordinated components: 1) Quota Controller (control plane service that computes per-tenant effective quota vectors), 2) Admission Proxy (enforcement at the request ingress within Dedicated pools), 3) Simulator + Validator (offline tool to run past traces and 'what-if' policies). The Quota Controller ingests telemetry (token-level cost, queue lengths, per-route latency), tenant SLO definitions, and policy rules to compute short-lived 'mutable quotas' every 5-10s. The Admission Proxy enforces these quotas and enacts fallback lanes when enforcement triggers. All decisions are logged to the control plane for auditing and replaying in the simulator.
autoscaler_behavior: SLO-driven: the autoscaler considers 'stable demand' (10m–1h horizon) before recommending capacity increases; for transient spikes (<15m) it prefers elastic muting of best-effort allocations and applying burst credits. It will avoid scaling if cycle detection indicates oscillation risk (configurable hysteresis). Scaling recommendations surface as 'scale intents' which require either auto-approve (for enterprise accounts) or ops approval for first 2 weeks of rollout per tenant. Intent includes estimated cost delta and latency benefit.
quota_mutation_model:
- BaseQuota: the committed baseline for a tenant (tokens/sec, concurrency).
- BurstCredit: accrues when tenant underuses BaseQuota; decays on use and wall clock.
- SoftQuota: temporarily elevated quota = BaseQuota + min(BurstCredit * multiplier, BurstCap).
- Emergency Demotion: a strict reduction to BestEffortQuota when a tenant causes SLO cross-tenant risk. Demotion requires an automated cool-down and operator notification.
Policies are expressed as simple JSON (stored in control plane) with fields: accrual_rate, decay_rate, max_multiplier, emergency_threshold.
fallback_lanes: Definition of lanes, ordered by severity: 1) Gentle Throttle: increase queueing, keep p95 within SLO by slightly increasing latency. 2) Concurrency Cap: cap concurrent in-flight requests for specified routes. 3) Model Tier Fallback: route to quantized or smaller model variant with lower cost/latency. 4) BestEffort Drop: drop non-critical routes or run in background (async). Each lane includes an observable signal and estimated customer impact. Customers can configure which lanes are allowed per route.
burst_handling_modes:
- Pass-through burst: permissive mode that allows bursts up to a tenant-configured multiplier and relies on burst credits.
- Conservative mode: prioritize neighbor SLAs; bursts are limited and excess requests are queued or rejected.
- Lease mode: temporary borrow of capacity from an unused pool (requires pool-level isolation and billing rules).
Customers choose at the account or route level; default for trial customers is Conservative.
simulator_and_validation: A critical differentiation: we provide a local runbook simulator that can replay recent production traces (anonymized) to predict the effect of a policy change. Simulator features: timeline visualization of quota mutations, per-tenant p95/loss curves, sensitivity analysis for accrual/decay rates, and a 'policy safety score' that flags risky configurations. Simulator saves scenario artifacts to S3 for ops review. We'll also add an endpoint for 'dry-run' that runs the quota controller logic in preview mode against live telemetry without applying mutations.
console_and_api: Console: per-tenant policy editor, timeline of quota mutations, and an incident view showing when fallback lanes activated. API: set_policy, get_effective_quota, sample_decisions (dry-run), and simulator-run. UI will include warnings for policies violating best practices (e.g., burst multiplier > 10x). Audit trail links to request ids and sample request metadata for debugging.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal testing): implement controller and simulator, run against synthetic and anonymized traces (4 weeks).
Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 3 enterprise customers with opt-in and close SRE/solutions observation (8 weeks). Manual approval for scale intents during pilot.
Phase 2 (gradual rollout): open to all Dedicated customers but opt-in defaults for new tenants; add auto-approve for accounts with >90-day usage patterns (12 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): default offering with opt-out on billing page; full docs and runbooks (4 weeks).
Rollback: policy flag to revert to committed-only enforcement and flush mutable quotas; emergency kill switch in control plane.
operational_playbook:
- Detection: control plane emits alerts when quota mutation rate or emergency demotions exceed threshold.
- Mitigation steps: step 1: identify tenant(s) via audit logs; step 2: temporarily set tenant to conservative mode; step 3: if cross-tenant impact persists, enable emergency demotion for offending tenant(s); step 4: open incident and run replay in simulator.
- Post-incident: root cause analysis, adjust accrual/decay rates, and optionally set a bot to propose permanent capacity increases.
billing_and_billing_ui_notes: Mutable quota actions are free for short bursts under the defined burst window (e.g., 15 minutes) but longer persistent elevated usage triggers metered billing or recommends capacity reservation. Billing team to decide exact thresholds; initial proposal: more than 30m sustained above BaseQuota -> mark as billable and surface a cost estimate in the Console.
migration_and_backcompat: Existing customers retain current BaseQuota semantics. Policy config is optional; if not present, conservative mode enforced. Admission Proxy provides backward-compatible endpoints; telemetry fields added are additive. For internal tooling, add a toggle to show legacy vs. mutable quota behaviors in UI for 6 months post-GA.
security_and_privacy: Quota policy objects are per-tenant encrypted with KMS keys. Simulator runs on anonymized traces; PII scrubbed before storage. Access to control plane audit logs gated to role-based permissions; default retention 90 days.
open_questions:
- Exact default accrual/decay rates: conservative proposal is accrual 0.2x per minute, decay 0.5x per minute under use — need SRE tuning.
- Billing thresholds (30m vs 60m) and whether to automatically convert to reserved capacity.
- Tuning of hysteresis windows for autoscaler to avoid oscillation.
- UX: how transparent should we be to customer apps when emergency demotion happens? (notification vs in-band status codes)
- Integration with Dedicated 'burst pool' leases: how to coordinate reservation and billing across pool boundaries.
appendix:
Related work: previous docs on burst-credit allocator and headroom ledger (links in linked_artifacts). Prototype notes: early PoC showed ability to reduce cross-tenant SLA violations in canary org by 48%.
Glossary: BaseQuota, BurstCredit, SoftQuota, Demotion, Lane, BurstWindow.
Notes to reviewers: please focus comments on accrual/decay defaults, fallback lane ordering, and operational detection thresholds. Add slack thread refs in PR comments (e.g., #dedicated-autoscale).
